hypothesis: A one-way SIMD-prefix/scalar-suffix hybrid using bounded 64-byte ASCII blocks may amortize scan overhead versus the earlier 16-byte prefix hybrid. It skips a block only when all four SSE2 vectors are ASCII; otherwise the strict scalar decoder resumes at that block's known code-point boundary and validates the first high-bit byte rather than assuming it is a lead. Whether this granularity helps the official mixed-width n=65536 workload is unmeasured.
notes: This is a distinct 64-byte prefix-only hybrid, not T1 whole-buffer validation. The supplied catalog reports four distinct valid programs with no repeats; the current selected parent is the repeated 16-byte scan at 60.43 µs, while the earlier 16-byte prefix-only hybrid measured 39.98 µs. The repeated 64-byte scanner measured 81.00 µs, but it is not this one-way scan policy. The candidate has no controller measurement yet; official mixed-width and ASCII/malformed boundary checks should determine its result.
transformations: Replace repeated SIMD scans between decoded code points with a single bounded scan over complete 64-byte prefix blocks, each checked by four unaligned SSE2 loads.
Skip a 64-byte block only when all bytes are ASCII; otherwise leave the index at the block start for strict scalar validation of the suffix, including any leading ASCII and the first high-bit byte.
Retain scalar tail handling, UTF-8 validity behavior, run ABI, output, and thread budget.
